    Unbounded preprojective components make the Euler form not weakly positive #

    Over an algebraically closed field a directing module has End M = k (Directing.finrank_end), so χ(dim M) = 1 (euler_directing). If a preprojective component has members of every dimension, their dimension vectors are infinitely many positive roots of the Euler form, which is therefore not weakly positive by Drozd's finiteness (not_weaklyPositive_of_unbounded).

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.AR.Directing.finrank_end {k A : Type u} [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] [IsAlgClosed k] {M : FDMod k A} (hM : Directing M) :
    Module.finrank k (M.carrier →ₗ[A] M.carrier) = 1

    A directing module over an algebraically closed field has End M = k.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.AR.not_weaklyPositive_of_unbounded {k A : Type u} [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (D : DirData k A) [IsAlgClosed k] (hT : ∀ (x : D.ι), x ∈ D.T) {𝒞 : FDMod k A → Prop} (h𝒞 : PreprojComp 𝒞) (hunb : ∀ (b : ℕ), ∃ (X : FDMod k A), 𝒞 X ∧ b < Module.finrank k X.carrier) :
    ¬(eulerForm D hT).WeaklyPositive
